# `validation/` — building, running and regression-testing LSSEFT-analytic

This directory contains everything needed to build `LSSEFT-analytic`, run it in the configuration
that reproduces its published output, and check that a change to the code did not alter that
output. It assumes **no prior knowledge of the repository**.

If you only read one thing, read §1 and §5.

---

## 0. What this program is, in two sentences

`LSSEFT-analytic` is a symbolic-computation program (C++ / GiNaC). It does not compute numbers: it
*emits C++ source code* — a directory called `autogenerated/` containing 22 `.cpp` files, of which
the important one is `kernel_integrands.cpp` holding **101 one-loop integrand kernels** — which is
then compiled into a separate numerical code. The published 2018 output is preserved at
`~/Documents/Code/LSSEFT/autogenerated/`.

Because the program's product is source code, "did I break it?" means "does it still emit the same
integrands?", and that is what the tooling here answers.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Need | Notes |
|---|---|
| A C++17 compiler | Apple clang 21.0.0 / arm64 is what this was last built with |
| CMake ≥ 3.16 | |
| GiNaC + CLN, discoverable by `pkg-config` | `pkg-config --modversion ginac` must work. Last measured: GiNaC 1.8.10, CLN 1.3.7 (MacPorts, `/opt/local`) |
| Python 3 with `sympy` and `mpmath` | Only for the comparison scripts, not for the build. Last measured: 3.14.4 / SymPy 1.14.0 / mpmath 1.4.0 |

**There is no Boost dependency.** It was removed in prompt 01 of the
`prompts/pre-python-migration-fixes/` campaign. If you find a `FIND_PACKAGE(Boost ...)`, you are on
an old commit.

---

## 2. Build

```bash
./validation/build.sh                 # -> build-validation/LSSEFT_analytic
./validation/build.sh /path/to/dir    # or somewhere else
```

Out-of-tree, `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`, idempotent — re-running reconfigures and rebuilds in
place. Nothing outside the build directory is written. `build-validation/` is gitignored.

---

## 3. Run

```bash
./validation/run.sh                        # -> validation/out/<UTC timestamp>{,.log}
./validation/run.sh /path/to/outdir        # explicit output directory
./validation/run.sh /path/to/outdir /path/to/builddir
```

`run.sh` invokes the **canonical configuration** — the one that reproduces the 2018 published
output:

```bash
./LSSEFT_analytic --no-auto-symmetrize --symmetrize-22 --counterterms --output <dir>
```

Stdout and stderr go to `<outdir>.log`, which carries the stage timings, the warnings and the
counterterm map. Expect ~45 s of user CPU and ~35 MB peak RSS. `validation/out/` is gitignored.

> ### ⚠ Do not just run `./LSSEFT_analytic --counterterms`
>
> **`--auto-symmetrize` is the tool's default**, and `run.sh` deliberately turns it off. The
> feasibility study measured the default at **19 m 02 s against 43 s — about 26× slower — for an
> identical counterterm map.** Prompt 02 re-measured it; see §8 for what was found. Unless you are
> specifically testing the symmetrizer, always use `run.sh` or pass `--no-auto-symmetrize`
> explicitly. The default costs you twenty minutes and buys you nothing.

Sanity checks on a fresh run:

```bash
OUT=validation/out/<timestamp>
ls "$OUT/autogenerated" | wc -l                                                           # 22
grep -c "double value_" "$OUT/autogenerated/kernel_integrands.cpp"                        # 101
grep -o 'compute_[A-Za-z0-9_]*' "$OUT/autogenerated/Pk_expressions.cpp" | sort -u | wc -l # 135
grep -c warning "$OUT.log"                                                                # 3
```

---

## 4. Do not use `diff` as your regression test

Two runs of the same binary with identical flags produce **different** `autogenerated/` trees.
Ten of the 22 files differ, `kernel_integrands.cpp` among them. The kernels are the same kernels;
they are numbered and ordered differently, because GiNaC 1.8.10 seeds its expression hash from a
runtime address and that hash propagates into the two `std::unordered_map`s that drive kernel
naming and file emission order.

This is measured, explained and anchored to file:line in **`validation/NONDETERMINISM.md`**. Read
it before you conclude that something is broken.

---

## 5. Compare two trees — the actual regression test

```bash
python3 validation/compare_autogenerated.py A/autogenerated B/autogenerated
```

Exit status **0 = match, 1 = mismatch, 2 = usage/parse error**, so it drops straight into a script.

What it does: extracts each kernel's `value_` and `Wick_` expression, parses them into SymPy with
**exact rational literals**, substitutes a surrogate power spectrum for `data_->Pk(·)`, evaluates
each kernel at 25 fixed seeded pseudo-random exact-rational `(k_, q_, z_)` points in mpmath at 60
digits, and compares the **multisets** of the resulting signature vectors. Multisets, not per-kernel
maps — so kernel renumbering and GiNaC term ordering cannot make it fail. It also compares the
`compute_*` name sets of `Pk_expressions.cpp`.

Typical output:

```
signatures matched: 101 of 101 (A) / 101 (B)
compute_* name sets: IDENTICAL (135 names)
RESULT: MATCH -- the two trees define the same integrands as functions.
```

On failure it names the `kerNNN` labels carrying each unmatched signature, on each side, so you can
go and look at the two `double value_` lines.

### Comparing against the archived baseline

You do not need to re-run the old code. The pre-fix signature multiset is stored:

```bash
python3 validation/compare_autogenerated.py \
    validation/out/<fresh>/autogenerated \
    --signatures validation/baselines/pre-fix/signatures.json
```

The stored file records the seed and the evaluation points; the script refuses to compare if the
evaluation-point policy has since changed, rather than silently producing a meaningless answer.

### The evaluation-point policy

Every constant lives in one clearly marked block at the top of `compare_autogenerated.py`:
seed `20260904`, 25 points, exact rationals over the prime denominator `1000003`, with
`k_ ∈ [0.05, 1)`, `q_ ∈ [0.05, 5)`, `z_ ∈ [-0.9, 0.9)`, mpmath 60 digits, signature key at 25
significant digits, fallback relative tolerance `1e-20`, surrogate `P(k) = k/(7k⁴ + 3k² + 1)`.

**Changing any of them invalidates every stored signature file.** If you must, re-baseline and say
so in the campaign log.

---

## 6. Canonical form and the duplicate diagnostic

```bash
python3 validation/canonical_form.py --dedup validation/out/<run>/autogenerated
python3 validation/canonical_form.py --show ker42 validation/out/<run>/autogenerated
python3 validation/canonical_form.py --counterterm-map validation/out/<run>.log
```

`canonical_form.py` is also the shared parsing layer that `compare_autogenerated.py` imports: it
knows the regexes for the emitted kernel shape, the C++→Python rewrites, and the exact-rational
parse. It fails loudly on any identifier it has not been taught, rather than mis-parsing quietly.

`--counterterm-map` is the third mode: it prints the run log's `** COUNTERTERM MAP` section with
each entry's *print order* canonicalised, which is the only way to compare that section between
runs (it is default-printed, so GiNaC's per-process operand ordering varies inside each line and
sorting the lines achieves nothing — measured, `NONDETERMINISM.md` §3.2). The canonicalised form is
a single md5 across all five runs of the non-determinism study and the `--auto-symmetrize` run.
It canonicalises print order only and does no algebra, so a real change still shows up.

`--dedup` reduces each `value_` with `cancel(together(·))`, keys it jointly with the raw `Wick_`
string, and reports how many kernels are algebraically distinct. Current answer:

```
emitted:  101
distinct after cancel(together(.)), keyed with Wick_: 95
duplicate groups: 6
```

Six of the 101 emitted kernels are exact algebraic duplicates that the emitter's string-hash dedup
misses. This is a **diagnostic, not a gate** — it exits 0 whatever it finds, unless you pass
`--expect 101:95:6`. It is issue **I-05** and is deliberately out of scope for the current campaign:
changing the dedup key would change the emitted artefact this oracle exists to validate against.

---

## 7. The archived baseline

`validation/baselines/pre-fix/` is the reference output as of the start of the campaign's
behavioural work:

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `autogenerated/` | the full emitted tree from one canonical run |
| `run.log` | that run's stdout+stderr, verbatim |
| `manifest.json` | commit, command line, compiler / GiNaC / CMake / Python versions, host, date, wall clock, per-file md5s, and the headline measurements |
| `signatures.json` | the integrand signature multiset, with the seed and the 25 points |
| `warnings.txt` | the warning set, ANSI codes and timestamps stripped |
| `counterterm-map.canonical.txt` | the counterterm map with each entry's print order canonicalised — the form that **is** comparable between runs (one md5 across six independent processes) |
| `counterterm-map.sorted-lines.txt` | the raw sorted-lines form, kept for reference and clearly labelled as **not** usable for comparison (four distinct md5s in five runs) |

The commit carrying it is tagged **`baseline/pre-fix`**.

### Re-baselining

Only do this when a prompt says to, and record the before/after in its log.

```bash
./validation/build.sh
./validation/run.sh "$PWD/validation/out/newbase"

B=validation/baselines/<name>
mkdir -p "$B"
cp -R validation/out/newbase/autogenerated "$B/autogenerated"
cp validation/out/newbase.log "$B/run.log"

python3 validation/compare_autogenerated.py --quiet "$B/autogenerated" \
        --emit-signatures "$B/signatures.json"

python3 validation/canonical_form.py --counterterm-map "$B/run.log" \
        > "$B/counterterm-map.canonical.txt"

# warnings.txt and counterterm-map.sorted-lines.txt: the exact shell pipelines are recorded as
# comment headers inside each of the corresponding files in validation/baselines/pre-fix/.
```

Then write `manifest.json` recording at minimum the commit SHA, the exact command line, the
compiler and GiNaC versions, the host, the date and the wall clock.

---

## 8. `--auto-symmetrize`: measured, and not worth it

Measured on this machine, 4 September 2026 — the same canonical output directory contents, produced
two ways:

| | `--no-auto-symmetrize` (what `run.sh` does) | `--auto-symmetrize` (the tool's default) |
|---|---|---|
| Wall clock | 50.9 s | **19 m 34 s** |
| User CPU | 45.3 s | **18 m 34 s** |
| Peak RSS | 33 MB | 120 MB |
| Kernels / `compute_*` names | 101 / 135 | 101 / 135 |
| Warnings | the same 3 | the same 3 |
| Counterterm map, canonicalised | identical md5 | identical md5 |
| Functional signature multiset | — | **101 of 101 matched** |

**23× the wall clock for an identical answer.** Use `run.sh`.

One caveat if you ever do run it: the emitted *text* is not the same — 80 of the 101
`double value_` lines and 53 of the 101 `double Wick_` lines are written differently, because the
symmetrizer builds differently-ordered (but algebraically identical) expression trees. Only the
functional comparison sees that correctly; `diff` would report ~130 spurious changes. Details in
`validation/NONDETERMINISM.md` §8.
